subproblems.title: An n-covector on vectors spanned by an orthonormal n-frame is det(⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩) times its value on the frame
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) (indexed by Fin n) be an orthonormal family in ℝᴾ = Euclid P and let b = (b₁, …, bₙ) be a family in ℝᴾ with bⱼ ∈ span{τ₁, …, τₙ} for every j. Then for every n-covector α of ℝᴾ (α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n, a continuous alternating n-linear form), α(b₁, …, bₙ) = det(𝒜)·α(τ₁, …, τₙ), where 𝒜 is the n×n real matrix 𝒜ᵢⱼ := ⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩ (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (b j)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ b : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (∀ j, b j ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ)) → ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, α b = (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (b j)).det * α τ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3(i) of the parent proof (the restriction α_L of α to L is a multiple of the basis determinant of L, evaluated at b), stated for an arbitrary orthonormal frame τ of the subspace L = span(range τ) containing b.
Notation: ℝᵐ means Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m); ⟨x, y⟩ is inner ℝ x y; e_j := EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ) is the j-th standard basis vector of ℝⁿ; an n-covector of ℝᴾ is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n = Euclid P [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ (a continuous alternating n-linear map ℝᴾ × ⋯ × ℝᴾ → ℝ); MultiVector P n = Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ (continuous linear functionals on n-covectors); for a continuous linear map F, F* = F.adjoint and det of an endomorphism is ContinuousLinearMap.det (= LinearMap.det of the underlying linear map). L := span ℝ (range τ) ⊆ ℝᴾ, an n-family c in L has underlying ambient family ↑c.
1. A basis of L indexed by Fin n. An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so τ is a basis of its span: e := Module.Basis.span hτ.linearIndependent is a basis (e₁, …, eₙ) of L whose underlying vectors are ↑eᵢ = τᵢ (Module.Basis.span_apply).
2. Restriction of α to L. Let α_L := α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap L.subtype, i.e. α_L(c₁, …, cₙ) := α(↑c₁, …, ↑cₙ) for cᵢ ∈ L; it is an alternating n-linear form on L. Put b'ⱼ := ⟨bⱼ, hbⱼ⟩ ∈ L (hypothesis). Then α(b) = α_L(b') and α(τ) = α(↑e) = α_L(e) (both by unfolding, using ↑eᵢ = τᵢ).
3. Alternating n-forms on the n-dimensional space L with basis e are multiples of the basis determinant: α_L = α_L(e) • det_e (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at b' gives α_L(b') = α_L(e)·det_e(b').
4. The coordinate matrix. det_e(b') = det M with Mᵢⱼ := e.repr(b'ⱼ)ᵢ (Module.Basis.det_apply, Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply). We claim Mᵢⱼ = ⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩. Indeed b'ⱼ = Σₗ Mₗⱼ • eₗ (Module.Basis.sum_repr); taking underlying vectors (Submodule.coe_sum, Submodule.coe_smul) gives bⱼ = Σₗ Mₗⱼ • τₗ, and taking the inner product with τᵢ and using orthonormality, ⟨τᵢ, Σₗ Mₗⱼ τₗ⟩ = Mᵢⱼ (Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype). Hence M = 𝒜.
5. Combining steps 2–4: α(b) = α_L(b') = α_L(e)·det_e(b') = α(τ)·det 𝒜 = det(𝒜)·α(τ). ∎
(The argument is uniform in n; for n = 0 both sides reduce to α of the empty family, det of the empty matrix being 1.)

  intro P n τ b hτ hb α
  set L := Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) with hLdef
  let e : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ L := Module.Basis.span hτ.linearIndependent
  have he : ∀ i, (e i : Euclid P) = τ i := fun i => by
    rw [Module.Basis.span_apply hτ.linearIndependent i]
  let αL : L [⋀^Fin n]→ₗ[ℝ] ℝ := α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap L.subtype
  let b' : Fin n → L := fun j => ⟨b j, hb j⟩
  have h1 : α b = αL b' := rfl
  have h2 : α τ = αL e := by
    show α τ = α (fun i => (e i : Euclid P))
    congr 1
    funext i
    exact (he i).symm
  -- coordinates of b' in e are the inner products with τ
  have hrepr : ∀ i j, e.repr (b' j) i = inner ℝ (τ i) (b j) := by
    intro i j
    have hs : (b j : Euclid P) = ∑ l, e.repr (b' j) l • τ l := by
      have := congrArg (Subtype.val) (e.sum_repr (b' j))
      simp only [Submodule.coe_sum, Submodule.coe_smul, he] at this
      exact this.symm
    rw [hs, hτ.inner_right_fintype]
  have hmat : e.toMatrix b' = Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (b j) := by
    ext i j
    rw [Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply, hrepr, Matrix.of_apply]
  have h3 : αL b' = αL e * e.det b' := by
    conv_lhs => rw [AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det e αL]
    rfl
  rw [h1, h2, h3, Module.Basis.det_apply, hmat, mul_comm]
proof_key_steps: τ orthonormal ⇒ linearly independent ⇒ basis e := Module.Basis.span of L = span(range τ) with ↑eᵢ = τᵢ.
Restrict α to L: α_L := α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap L.subtype; α(b) = α_L(b') and α(τ) = α_L(e).
AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det: α_L = α_L(e)·det_e, so α(b) = α(τ)·det_e(b').
det_e(b') = det of the coordinate matrix, whose (i,j) entry is ⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩ by expanding bⱼ = Σₗ cₗ τₗ and orthonormality.
Hence α(b) = det(⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩)·α(τ).

subproblems.title: Gram determinant: det(F*∘F) is the square of the frame-coordinate determinant
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, F : ℝⁿ → ℝᴾ a continuous linear map and τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) an orthonormal family in ℝᴾ such that F eⱼ ∈ span{τ₁, …, τₙ} for every j, where eⱼ = EuclideanSpace.single j 1 is the standard basis of ℝⁿ. Then det(F*∘F) = (det 𝒜)², where F* is the adjoint of F, det(F*∘F) is the determinant of the endomorphism F.adjoint ∘L F of ℝⁿ (ContinuousLinearMap.det), and 𝒜ᵢⱼ := ⟨τᵢ, F eⱼ⟩.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (∀ j, F (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)) ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ)) → (F.adjoint ∘L F).det = (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (F (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)))).det ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3(ii) and 3(iii) of the parent proof (Gram matrix Γ = 𝒜ᵀ𝒜 and det A(v) = det Γ), stated for an arbitrary continuous linear map F and an orthonormal frame τ whose span contains the vectors F eⱼ.
Notation: ℝᵐ means Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m); ⟨x, y⟩ is inner ℝ x y; e_j := EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ) is the j-th standard basis vector of ℝⁿ; an n-covector of ℝᴾ is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n = Euclid P [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ (a continuous alternating n-linear map ℝᴾ × ⋯ × ℝᴾ → ℝ); MultiVector P n = Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ (continuous linear functionals on n-covectors); for a continuous linear map F, F* = F.adjoint and det of an endomorphism is ContinuousLinearMap.det (= LinearMap.det of the underlying linear map). Write bⱼ := F eⱼ and 𝒜ᵢⱼ := ⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩.
1. Expansion in the frame. Fix j. Since bⱼ ∈ span(range τ) there are reals cₗ with bⱼ = Σₗ cₗ • τₗ (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun). For each l, orthonormality gives ⟨τₗ, Σₘ cₘ τₘ⟩ = cₗ (Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype), i.e. 𝒜ₗⱼ = cₗ. Hence bⱼ = Σₗ 𝒜ₗⱼ • τₗ.
2. Gram matrix. For all i, j, by step 1 applied to bᵢ and bilinearity (sum_inner, inner_smul_left; real scalars): ⟨bᵢ, bⱼ⟩ = ⟨Σₗ 𝒜ₗᵢ τₗ, bⱼ⟩ = Σₗ 𝒜ₗᵢ ⟨τₗ, bⱼ⟩ = Σₗ 𝒜ₗᵢ 𝒜ₗⱼ = (𝒜ᵀ𝒜)ᵢⱼ (Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply).
3. Matrix of F*∘F. Let B := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis, the standard basis of ℝⁿ (Bⱼ = eⱼ), whose coordinate functionals are B.repr(x)ᵢ = xᵢ = ⟨eᵢ, x⟩ (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_repr, EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left). The (i, j) entry of the matrix of the linear map F*∘F in the basis B is (F*(F eⱼ))ᵢ = ⟨eᵢ, F*(F eⱼ)⟩ = ⟨F eᵢ, F eⱼ⟩ (LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right) = (𝒜ᵀ𝒜)ᵢⱼ by step 2. So LinearMap.toMatrix B B (F*∘F) = 𝒜ᵀ𝒜.
4. Determinant. ContinuousLinearMap.det is LinearMap.det of the underlying linear map, and the determinant of a linear endomorphism is the determinant of its matrix in any basis (LinearMap.det_toMatrix). Therefore det(F*∘F) = det(𝒜ᵀ𝒜) = det(𝒜ᵀ)·det(𝒜) = (det 𝒜)² (Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_transpose). ∎

subproblems.title: The range of an injective linear map ℝⁿ → ℝᴾ has an orthonormal frame indexed by Fin n
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let F : ℝⁿ → ℝᴾ be an injective continuous linear map. Then there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) in ℝᴾ, indexed by Fin n, whose span equals the range of F: span ℝ (range τ) = LinearMap.range (F : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n →L[ℝ] Euclid P), Injective F → ∃ τ : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ τ ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) = LinearMap.range (F : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof ("choose an orthonormal basis τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) of L indexed by Fin n (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ L reindexed along finrank L = n; regard τᵢ ∈ ℝ^{n+k})"), stated for an arbitrary injective F.
Notation: ℝᵐ means Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m); ⟨x, y⟩ is inner ℝ x y; e_j := EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ) is the j-th standard basis vector of ℝⁿ; an n-covector of ℝᴾ is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n = Euclid P [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ (a continuous alternating n-linear map ℝᴾ × ⋯ × ℝᴾ → ℝ); MultiVector P n = Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ (continuous linear functionals on n-covectors); for a continuous linear map F, F* = F.adjoint and det of an endomorphism is ContinuousLinearMap.det (= LinearMap.det of the underlying linear map).
1. Dimension. Let L := range F, a submodule of ℝᴾ. Since F is injective, finrank L = finrank ℝⁿ = n (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).
2. An orthonormal basis of L indexed by Fin n. L with the inner product of ℝᴾ is a finite-dimensional inner product space; its standard orthonormal basis stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ L is indexed by Fin (finrank L); reindexing along finrank L = n (OrthonormalBasis.reindex (finCongr h)) gives an orthonormal basis T = (T₁, …, Tₙ) of L.
3. Orthonormality in ℝᴾ. Put τᵢ := ↑Tᵢ ∈ ℝᴾ, i.e. τ = L.subtype ∘ T. The inclusion L → ℝᴾ is a linear isometry (L.subtypeₗᵢ), and an orthonormal family stays orthonormal under a linear isometry (Orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry), so τ is orthonormal.
4. Span. range τ is the image of range T under the inclusion (Set.range_comp), so span(range τ) is the image of span(range T) under the inclusion (Submodule.span_image). T spans L (its underlying basis satisfies Module.Basis.span_eq; OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis), so span(range T) = ⊤ and its image is the range of the inclusion, which is L (Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype). Hence span(range τ) = L = range F. ∎
